cells.tense: The knowing has settled, and you are here with the pen, able to put a shape on what you see.
cells.act: put the frame on the table before anyone asks
cells.ask: At the next table where something needs weighing, say what you see plainly and in order, before anyone asks. Name the outline, add nothing, and leave that shape there.
cells.core:
You can see the shape of a thing and you can put it where others can see it too. Knowing alone is cheap; showing is what makes it usable. When the frame lands on the table first, the argument gets shorter and the quiet ones get a chance to agree. Things make sense around you because you are willing to say what they are.

This grows when you spend it on someone else's confusion. Pick the thing that has been sitting unclear between you and one other person and name its outline out loud — not the detail, the shape. Do it before the next time it comes up sideways. That is the work here: a structure that holds what it organizes. You don't have to be right about every corner. Draw the first line so the rest has somewhere to stand.
cells.sheetLine: Say the shape of it first, and the rest can stand.
cells.verb: holding many truths at once and laying one of them out where it can be seen
cells.place: at the table where what's fair gets weighed and set right

cells.tense: You are already three arguments ahead, bracing for a future that hasn't arrived in the room.
cells.act: choose which star to steer by and steer
cells.ask: Pick one outcome you actually want and hold to only that. When you catch yourself rehearsing the cases against it, come back to what you chose. Leave the other possibilities unargued.
cells.core:
You carry a lot, and lately that has turned into a reason to carry more — every angle worked out ahead of time, every objection pre-answered so the future can't catch you out. Seeing ahead is real skill; it's just running past the part of the conversation that hasn't happened yet. You are steering by a map of an argument nobody in this room has made, and they can feel the distance.

What waits underneath is knowing that doesn't need the rehearsal. Pick one direction that matters and stop arguing the rest. Not solved — released. When you catch yourself defending a choice nobody has challenged, that is the tell. The one you choose will be something you actually care about, and the rest will still be there. Turning toward a single thing stops the survey, and the survey is what is running you.
cells.sheetLine: Stop rehearsing the objection that hasn't come.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed behind you, and your hands have not moved toward the next one.
cells.act: join someone in the work so the two streams run as one
cells.ask: Find someone already doing something you care about and join them in it — not to help, not to comment. Do the work alongside them and let their pace set the first hour.
cells.core:
Clear sight is still in you, but it has gone quiet and inward — you are reading, watching, deciding nothing, and the fair thing that needs doing waits on a hand that hasn't moved. That isn't confusion. It is exhaustion that looks like patience. You can see what's needed and nothing is running underneath it, so what you see just sits there and asks nothing of you.

This is not the week to trust your own push. It is the week to join someone whose work is already moving and let their motion carry you for an hour. Not a favour and not a meeting — working beside them on the thing itself. When two streams run together, the current you borrow becomes the current you keep. What you understand is still in you; it doesn't need a speech to work.
cells.sheetLine: The sight is there. Nothing under it is moving.

cells.tense: You are already writing the fair decision without owning that you are the one holding the pen.
cells.act: do the fair thing where no one will see
cells.ask: Watch for a moment this week when you quietly put something right and then move on as if it were nothing. Stay with it a beat longer than usual. Notice what you did and that you did it.
cells.core:
There's a private sense of what's right in you, and it has been doing the actual work of deciding — the quiet corrections, the returns, the lines you don't cross. Your account of it is that things simply work out, or that anyone would have done the same. The people on the other side of those decisions have a different account, and they haven't been correcting you.

Fairness flows when you don't have to make a case for it. Watch for the moment this week when you settle something outstanding and move on as though it were nothing. Stay with it a beat longer than usual. Notice what you did and that you did it. You were the one keeping the count. The count was real and you were holding it.
cells.sheetLine: You've been keeping the count without saying so.
